sa: तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव ॥
tr: tatkiṃ karmaṇi ghore māṃ niyojayasi keśava
en: Janardana, if you hold that understanding is greater than action, then why, Keshava, do you urge me into this terrible deed?
speaker: Arjuna said

en: With words that seem to point two ways, you confuse my mind. Tell me, decisively, the one path by which I may reach the highest good.
Sinless one, as I said before, there are two paths in this world: the path of knowledge for those given to contemplation, and the path of action for those given to yoga.
speaker: Krishna said

en: No one reaches freedom from action simply by not beginning it, and no one attains perfection by renunciation alone.
No one can remain without acting even for a moment. Everyone is driven to act, helplessly, by the qualities born of nature.

sa: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन्।
tr: karmendriyāṇi saṃyamya ya āste manasā smaran
en: Whoever restrains the organs of action but sits dwelling on sense objects in the mind is deluded, and is called a hypocrite.
But whoever governs the senses with the mind, Arjuna, and without attachment takes up the yoga of action with the organs of action, excels.

sa: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः।
tr: niyataṃ kuru karma tvaṃ karma jyāyo hyakarmaṇaḥ
en: Do the work that is yours, for action is better than inaction. Without action, even the upkeep of your body would not be possible.
This world is bound by action, except action done as an offering (yajna). So, son of Kunti, act for that purpose, free from attachment.
In the beginning the Creator brought forth beings together with sacrifice and said: by this you shall flourish; let it be the cow that grants your wishes.
Nourish the gods with this, and let the gods nourish you. Nourishing one another, you will reach the highest good.

sa: तैर्दत्तानप्रदायैभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स्तेन एव सः ॥
tr: tairdattānapradāyaibhyo yo bhuṅkte stena eva saḥ
en: Nourished by sacrifice, the gods will give you the enjoyments you desire. Whoever enjoys their gifts without offering anything back is simply a thief.

sa: भुञ्जते ते त्वघं पापा ये पचन्त्यात्मकारणात् ॥
tr: bhuñjate te tvaghaṃ pāpā ye pacantyātmakāraṇāt
en: The good, who eat what remains after the offering, are freed of all wrongs; but those who cook only for themselves eat sin.
Beings come from food, food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice is born of action.
Know that action arises from the Veda, and the Veda from the Imperishable. So the all-pervading Brahman is ever present in sacrifice.
Whoever does not keep turning the wheel set in motion this way lives in sin, delighting only in the senses; that life is lived in vain, Partha.

sa: आत्मन्येव च सन्तुष्टस्तस्य कार्यं न विद्यते ॥
tr: ātmanyeva ca santuṣṭastasya kāryaṃ na vidyate
en: But for one who delights in the Self alone, who is satisfied in the Self and content in the Self, there is nothing left that must be done.
Such a person has nothing to gain by acting here, nothing to lose by not acting, and depends on no being for anything.
So always do the work that must be done, without attachment. By acting without attachment, a person reaches the Supreme.
Janaka and others reached perfection through action alone. Keeping in view the welfare of the world (lokasangraha), you too should act.
Whatever the best person does, others follow. Whatever standard they set, the world goes by it.

sa: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किञ्चन।
tr: na me pārthāsti kartavyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiñcana
en: Partha, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, nothing I lack that I need to gain; and yet I keep on acting.

sa: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः।
tr: yadi hyahaṃ na varteyaṃ jātu karmaṇyatandritaḥ
en: For if I ever stopped acting, tirelessly, people everywhere would follow my path, Partha.

sa: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम्।
tr: utsīdeyurime lokā na kuryāṃ karma cedaham
en: If I did not act, these worlds would fall into ruin; I would be the cause of chaos and would destroy these beings.
As the unwise act attached to their work, Bharata, so the wise should act, unattached, wishing to hold the world together.
The wise should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action. Acting with discipline themselves, they should inspire others to do all their work gladly.
All actions are carried out by the qualities of nature, but one whose mind is clouded by ego thinks, "I am the doer."

sa: गुणा गुणेषु वर्तन्त इति मत्वा न सज्जते ॥
tr: guṇā guṇeṣu vartanta iti matvā na sajjate
en: But one who knows the truth about the qualities and their workings, mighty-armed, sees that it is qualities moving among qualities, and is not attached.
Those deluded by the qualities of nature cling to their workings. One who knows the whole should not unsettle the slow of mind who know only a part.
Surrendering all actions to me, your mind on the Self, free from hope and from "mine," fight, with the fever gone.
Those who always follow this teaching of mine, with faith and without finding fault, are freed from the bonds of action.
But those who find fault with it and do not follow my teaching, know them to be confused about all knowledge, lost and without discernment.

sa: प्रकृतिं यान्ति भूतानि निग्रहः किं करिष्यति ॥
tr: prakṛtiṃ yānti bhūtāni nigrahaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati
en: Even the wise act according to their own nature. All beings follow their nature; what can mere suppression achieve?
Attraction and aversion sit waiting in every sense toward its object. Do not fall under their control; they are robbers on the road.
Better your own dharma, even done imperfectly, than another's done well. Better to die in your own dharma; another's dharma is full of fear.

sa: अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः।
tr: atha kena prayukto'yaṃ pāpaṃ carati pūruṣaḥ
en: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Varshneya, even against their own will, as if forced?
speaker: Arjuna said

en: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion (rajas): all-devouring and the great wrongdoer. Know it as the enemy here.
speaker: Krishna said

en: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an unborn child by the womb, so is this knowledge covered by desire.
Knowledge is veiled, son of Kunti, by this constant enemy of the wise, in the form of desire, a fire that can never be filled.
The senses, the mind and the intellect are said to be its seat. Through them it veils knowledge and deludes the embodied one.
So first master the senses, best of the Bharatas, and slay this sinful thing that destroys knowledge and wisdom.

sa: मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥
tr: manasastu parā buddhiryo buddheḥ paratastu saḥ
en: The senses are high, they say; higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is the intellect; and higher than the intellect is the Self.
Knowing what is higher than the intellect, steady the self by the Self, mighty-armed, and slay this enemy in the form of desire, so hard to conquer.
